spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: An infinite multiplicative support is compressed by capping how many primes a number may take from each scale block. The remaining square-free family is automatically divisor closed, and factorial/binomial estimates show its combinatorial entropy stays below log N.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The primes are partitioned into blocks P_k. Sets M_k contain numbers whose occupancy in block P_k exceeds a threshold, and M is the support of f with all such sets removed. Thus each element of M is square-free with bounded block occupancy, and M is divisor closed. Stirling-type factorial bounds, binomial estimates, and prime counts bound the product of blockwise choices and give |M|≤N for sufficiently large N.
directed.conceptual_reading: Block occupancy is a coarse sufficient statistic for support size. Capping it preserves downward divisibility while turning a multiplicative family into a product of finite combinatorial choices that can be entropy-bounded.

With N=floor(T^κ), the divisor-closed multiplicative set is partitioned into short logarithmic intervals; one representative is kept from each occupied interval and its coefficient aggregates nearby f(n)². The resulting support M′ has size at most N.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Divisor pairs with an excessively large complementary ratio are removed by turning the threshold into a fractional-power penalty. Multiplicativity then bounds the remaining divisor product uniformly over the compressed support, showing that frequency-incompatible arithmetic mass is negligible.

Uniform smallness of 1/(p^(1/4)f(p)) and the occupancy bound imply o(1).

Expanding |R|² turns it into a Fourier-weighted pair sum; rapid Gaussian-transform decay kills separated clusters, while only a bounded neighborhood of clusters survives and is charged to total multiplicative mass.
